title: Role of the noradrenergic system in the regulation of learning dynamics: evaluation of the effect of a low-dose selective noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor (NOISYXETINE)
official: Role of the noradrenergic system in the regulation of learning dynamics: evaluation of the effect of a low-dose selective noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor (NOISYXETINE)
summary: Main objective: To characterize the role of the noradrenergic system in the regulation of learning dynamics in healthy subjects, by comparing the behaviour of the subject during learning (in a stable accumulation task and in a changing accumulation task), their pupil diameter, and their electroencephalographic (EEG) responses, after taking a single dose of atomoxetine (40 mg) and placebo
conditions: Healthy subjects with no neurological or psychiatric disorders
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age 18 to 39 years old
2. Right-handed, assessed by the Edinburgh scale
3. Written signed informed consent
4. Subject covered by the social security system
Exclusion criteria:
1. Pregnant, parturient or breastfeeding woman
2. Person subject to a legal protection measure or unable to express consent
3. Known intolerance to atomoxetine
4. Need to wear glasses and/or lenses to obtain normal vision
5. Subject in an exclusion period or enrolled in an interventional study
6. First-degree family history of axis I disorder (DSM-IV-TR), excepted unipolar mood and anxiety disorders with OCD
7. Personal history of axis I disorder (DSM-IV-TR) in the 6 months preceding the study entry
8. Dependence on a psychoactive substance in the 12 months preceding the study entry, excluding nicotine, any behavioural disorder incompatible with a 2-hour electroencephalographic recording
9. Neuro/psychotropic treatment ongoing or stopped less than 1 month ago
10. Personal history of neurological pathology (e.g.: congenital malformation, benign or malignant tumour, degenerative disease of the central nervous system (CNS), epilepsy, inflammatory or infectious disease of the CNS, etc.)
11. Personal history of chronic disease of infectious, neoplastic, vascular, dysimmune or inflammatory, metabolic or endocrine, degenerative or genetic aetiology. In particular, angle-closure glaucoma, pheochromocytoma, known high blood pressure or measured blood pressure greater than 140/90 mm Hg at baseline, congenital heart disease, known ischemic heart disease, known heart failure, supraventricular or ventricular heart rhythm disorder, nephropathy, known liver disease and any pathology likely to be aggravated by an increase in blood pressure
12. Any medical treatment in the month preceding the study entry, apart from effective contraceptive treatment
13. Subject deprived of liberty by a judicial or administrative decision
